The claude driver against a fake Claude Code that speaks exactly the recorded print-mode exchanges: the request is the program's first line of input and never an argument, the result's answer and verdict are the work's, the permission maps to Claude Code's own modes, a command and a call of TTasks's tools report their progress, a permission prompt is declined and counted, a question for the person ends the run as needing the person with the question kept and a later one changes nothing, an unknown request gets the protocol's error, a signed-out program ends with its own words and the sign-in command, a helper agent in the background or a queued turn keeps the work open until the program's own turn, which can still ask, while a command left in the background does not, every final result settles the work before the input closes and at the same line however the output is chunked, Stop between turns, during the turn, during start-up and of a silent program, a program that does not exit after its work settles with its answer, a program that stops writing, and a whole answer after megabytes of other output

A Claude Code run in the run host with real processes, behind its npm shim, in a job object on Windows and without a process group everywhere: start to answer with the request on the program's input and on no command line, Stop during a turn and during start-up over the program's input, a program that does not exit after its work is ended with its answer kept, a process the agent left behind is ended and the cleanup says so, and nothing of a run is left alive

Zod and Ajv give the same verdict on every example and its mutations, and at the boundaries of every field, used by an example or not

Values fuzzed from each JSON Schema: Zod and Ajv agree, parseInput returns a value its schema accepts again unchanged, the agent input stays within the full input, every agent rule and default in the entry data takes effect, and every schema the registry check accepts, hostile probes included, holds all of these
Every generated JSON Schema is valid draft 2020-12, every entry's metadata is consistent and every result can express what its input asks for
The generated files match a fresh render and are byte-stable: LF, sorted keys, no timestamps, no absolute paths

Every verb whose contract says the command line fills base reads one for each of its writes by a read that writes nothing: the task it names or the bound task, or a read action of its own entry; a create needs none

The agent input built from an entry's rules drops hidden fields, requires the required ones and applies the agent limits by path, and mcp-tools.json lists only agent entries with an MCP face; the tools that create a task ask for an effort estimate on the default scale
SafeText strips tag, bidirectional, control and zero-width characters and normalises to NFC with LF; limits count code points and hold on the normalised text
The generated client posts to the generated routes and throws AppError on an error envelope

Driver contract suite: open, busy timeout first and A1's pragma order, statements, transactions, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, typed errors, close, missing and corrupt files, single-step backup into a new file only, and no ATTACH or VACUUM INTO of a named file
The start-up check asks the driver for its own SQLite, and a simulated build without FTS5, or with an old version, no JSON, no STRICT or no backup API, refuses to open
Connections in storage worker threads: the typed protocol, and a writer and two readers that start together open cleanly in repeated rounds

Schema lint on a freshly created space: every table STRICT, no forbidden column names, primary keys, the WITHOUT ROWID rule, ID and instant types, version maps, resolvable foreign keys, enum and JSON CHECKs that match the code and refuse bad values
ID property test: a typed prefix and 26 Crockford base32 characters that encode exactly the 128 bits of the OS random source, with one spelling per ID and strict validation

Short references: task references and entry ordinals format and parse as the contracts patterns do, the default prefix avoids taken ones, and allocation inside a transaction never reuses and stops at its range
Through the service, a change made at the command line is undone from the page after the service restarted, and redone at the command line: the undo history is the space's, shared by every client
Through the service, a claim of a restored copy goes on from its original's task references, and a restore in place goes on from the claimed copy's

Over random sequences of creates, backups and restores in place, no task reference is given to a second task; a backup from a later state keeps its counter, and a live space that does not open still lends its own

Create and open a space folder: space.json, schema 0.1, epoch 1 and a random incarnation, owner-only modes; refusals for an existing or missing folder, another database, a newer, unknown or inconsistent revision and a mismatched space_id, each leaving the database's bytes and journal mode as they were; a rollback journal or an empty database file refused before SQLite opens it; a change between inspection and the writer refused before any persistent pragma, and before the first read when the file system shows it; space.json rebuilt by the writer only when it is missing or stale

space.json's safety fields (space_id, format, min_reader, min_writer) are each read on their own and honoured whatever else is damaged; a damaged manifest (not a JSON object, too large, no marker, a safety field missing or invalid) makes the writer refuse and is never rewritten, and a reader reads on; app versions compare by SemVer precedence

An atomic file write writes every byte through short writes, removes its temporary file on any failure and throws the first error; a failing cleanup never replaces it, and no error carries a path or a native message
Space path rules: absolute, a portable slug as the folder name, and on Windows no trailing dot or space, reserved character or device name in any component
Row decoders refuse a bigint, a fraction, a wrong type or a value outside the guarded integer ranges, which match the contracts wire patterns
A backup taken under 10 writers restores into a new folder with a passing integrity_check, and last_seq and the counts equal the sidecar's; the snapshot is transactionally consistent

A backup is a single-step copy from a read-only connection, checked with integrity_check, compressed and read back, with a sidecar of the snapshot's facts and owner-only files under A1's name, reserved so that two backups never share or replace one name, in a backups folder synced into its parent when new
A crash at each point of a backup leaves either a complete backup or leftovers that are never listed as one, and the space untouched; a failure removes everything the backup wrote

Listing a space's backups: complete ones newest first, a missing or resized data file and an invalid sidecar by state, crash leftovers named and removable, only a backup's own files ever removed and only once untouched for an hour, sidecars found by path as a restore finds them, out-of-range names ignored

The shared BundlePolicy on .db.gz files: a highly compressible space round-trips; a database over the limit is refused before a backup writes and while a restore streams, leaving no folder; free disk space is checked

Daily backups are due after 03:00 local time or at start after 24 hours, a future-dated one aside; retention of one space's backups keeps 7 daily, 4 weekly, every backup that is not a daily one (manual, pre-migration), the newest complete backup, and never the newest that passes every check a restore makes; it removes only the regular files it listed

A backup publishes its data and its sidecar by a hard link or an exclusive create, never a rename: a pair or a part of one planted under its names while it runs is never replaced, its own files go, and without hard links the copies restore

Verified means a trial restore: a backup whose every check passes but whose restore fails at its first write (the read-only mark) is not verified, retention keeps the older backup that restores instead of removing it, a restore refuses the backup with BACKUP_INVALID and restore latest goes past it; the trials leave no file beside the backups

A reader opens both files of a backup before it reads either and reads only through them: retention removing a backup while its verification holds both files leaves the verification passing, and a restore whose files are removed after they are open restores the backup whole

The backup writer and the exporter check the shared free-space reserve against their estimated peak before they write anything: one byte short is BUNDLE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with no backups or exports folder made, exactly enough runs

Rotation removes only what A1's retention allows: a property test over random backup sets, clocks, offsets and commits removes only daily backups, never the one holding the furthest saved work, another space's or a damaged one; on real files manual backups, the newest verified one and a damaged newer one stay

A restore refuses an archive with `..`, an absolute or drive path, a backslash, empty or dot parts, device names or NFD, a link, device or FIFO by its attributes, a Windows reparse point, too many entries, too many expanded bytes declared or produced, an oversized file, duplicate names by case, a file where a folder is, overlapping entries, encryption, another method, an unknown or unlisted file, a wrong checksum or no archive at all, and leaves no folder

Export bundles in backup, fork and transfer mode hold the vacuumed snapshot, space.json, export.json, the live attachments' blobs and data.jsonl when asked, owner-only under A1's name; they restore as read-only copies; a changed bundle is refused; a fault before publication leaves nothing, after it the bundle stays; publication never replaces a file at its name, with or without hard links

The export's secret scan: an export that finds nothing writes its bundle; a secret-shaped string in any table, with or without data.jsonl, or in an attachment is a warning on the written bundle that names each kind and place once but never the text; the vacuumed snapshot holds no byte of text edited away; an attachment reached through a link into the secrets folder is refused

The largest stress-corpus bundle passes the shared BundlePolicy: 10,000 open and 100,000 completed tasks export with data.jsonl and restore with the same counts, and a projection-sized archive of 110,001 files reads under the policy through ZIP64's end records

The restore drill: a backup and an export bundle each restore into a new folder with a passing integrity_check and the live space's last_seq and counts, open read-only, and so does a copy of the restored folder; restored in place from the bundle the space is claimed with a new epoch and its old folder kept

entries.title: The two actions for a failed check through the CLI: restore latest restores the space's newest backup that verifies into a new folder as a read-only copy, skipping and keeping a newer one that does not; rescue writes every readable row into exchange/rescued; the read-only words name both and never a new backup

Rescue of a damaged database keeps the rows that can still be read from a private copy of its files: a table that fails partway is named by its product name, the others are written whole, every file of the space folder stays byte for byte (a write-ahead log beside an empty database, one with rows not checkpointed, a hot journal), a table the product does not have is neither written nor named, and each rescue writes a new file of its own

The secret patterns of A6 3.16.4 find each kind of token alone and inside text, and across a chunk boundary through the kept overlap, and leave ordinary words, short or digitless look-alikes and public keys unflagged
A migration whose barrier backup fails, at any point, never starts; a write between the backup and the migration stops it too; the space then opens read-only with the reason
A failed daily backup, or a newest backup that does not restore, is shown by doctor and the space list with its cause and what to run, through a running service, and goes when a backup succeeds again

Within one history of a space, the newest backup is the one holding the furthest saved work: a later commit, and a later time only for the same commit. After the clock was set back, restore latest takes the backup with the later commits, and retention and the upkeep keep it as the newest and as its day's

Each claim and restore in place starts a history of backups, and no history's backups are judged by another's: a daily of one copy does not stand for another's, retention keeps each history's newest backup that restores, restore latest takes the served copy's own history and, when it has none here, the one written to last while naming the others, and space backups tells the copies apart

Only a backup's own content makes it damaged, and any other failure is said as itself: an I/O error on the destination or SQLite out of memory stops restore latest instead of restoring older work, and a trial restore that the disk or its free space stops leaves the backup unchecked, so retention names no older backup the newest that restores and removes nothing

A space's backups go to a folder per space beside the TTasks home, never inside it, and are listed and restored from there only; files in the space's own backups folder are neither read nor removed; a folder there that cannot be made takes no backup elsewhere

Through the service, a backups folder set for the space that is not there is said as not there, with its path, by the backup list, restore latest, a backup now and the upkeep, and no backup makes a folder in its place: an upgrade waits, read-only at its revision with no backup anywhere and nothing recorded, and migrates at the next open once the folder is back; restore latest from a folder with no backup of the space says there is none

A rescue takes only the rows of the space it is for: a folder whose database names another space is refused with no rows file, also through the service when another space's folder took the registered one's place, and a database too damaged to say which space it holds is rescued and says so

The upkeep removes only a backup's own temporary files: a backup's data whose sidecar is missing stays, listed as such, and restores once its sidecar is back; a backup taken before an upgrade stays until the person removes it

A migration starts only behind a barrier backup that passes a trial restore: one that reads back but does not restore, or a full disk at the trial restore, stops it, and the space stays readable at its revision

The migration runner from 0.1 through the real 0.2 and 0.3 and a stand-in 0.4: one system commit per step, user_version, format, undo floor and space.json; a step that fails midway, in its verify or on a foreign key leaves the space at its revision, and it still opens

The 0.1 fixture (the Mira sample built by the 0.1 chain, with the 0.1 builds' digest) migrates to the build's latest revision behind its verified barrier backup: every 0.1 row stays, one migration commit per step, the new tables empty but the search index, which holds the tasks, the schema equal to a new space's and to the pinned released schema, and the barrier backup restores the fixture's counts, last_seq and rows

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.1 to 0.2 migration (the 0.2 chain), one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the fixture's, it opens read-only with A1's message, the 0.1 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

An older build refuses to open a 0.2 space writable: the 0.1 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.2 backup

The 0.2 fixture (the Mira sample built by the 0.2 chain, with a row in every 0.2 table) migrates to 0.3 behind its verified barrier backup: every 0.2 row stays, one migration commit, the sessions and runs tables empty, the schema equal to a new 0.3 space's and to the pinned 0.3 schema, and the barrier backup restores the fixture's counts, last_seq and rows

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.2 to 0.3 migration, one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the 0.2 fixture's, it opens read-only with A1's message, the 0.2 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

A 0.2 build refuses to open a 0.3 space writable: the 0.2 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.3 backup

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.3 to 0.4 migration, the search index's fill included, one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the 0.3 sample's, it opens read-only with the failure's message, the 0.3 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

A 0.3 build refuses to open a 0.4 space writable: the 0.3 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.4 backup

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.4 to 0.5 migration, one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the 0.4 sample's, it opens read-only with the failure's message, the 0.4 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

A 0.4 build refuses to open a 0.5 space writable: the 0.4 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.5 backup

Areas and projects through the write path: create with a slug from the title, numbered when taken, in one request with a task filed into the new project; rename and other fields with a base, keeping the ID, slug and tasks; a project moved to another area with all its tasks; archive and unarchive, idempotent, keeping the group's tasks as they are; delete refused while a project holds tasks, delete and restore of an empty one; an undo of a create archives the group with what is in it, and its redo and an unarchive's undo

Folders through the write path: a project created with its folder in one commit whose undo archives it and keeps its folder, the path stored exactly as sent; a moved folder, with a base, carrying every folder inside it, other projects' and their tasks' too, in one change, a task's moved folder carrying a project's inside it, and a change without carry changing the owner's folder alone; any number of live projects on one folder, a move landing a project on another's folder and one sharing the moved folder moving with it; a project's delete removing its folders on every machine and its restore from the Trash bringing them back beside a project that took one meanwhile; a folder changed to one inside or around the old one moves no task folder, a deleted task's moves with a real move; a stale base meets a folder the move would carry or a folder cleared since as a conflict; a deleted project never holds a live folder or task, through a task's restore or several operations of one request; one request changes an owner's folder once; a task's folder set, changed and cleared; paths the request's machine cannot name refused

Property tests over random folder sets and clears, task moves, deletes and restores, project moves, deletes and restores, undos and redos between them on a Linux and a Windows machine, with an agent's changes between: one live folder per owner and machine, any number of projects on one folder, a deleted project holds no live folder or task and a task is in its project's area, a project's or a task's moved folder carries exactly every other folder inside the old one on that machine, and a change without carry the owner's folder alone, by an oracle of the test's own, and the history invariants hold

A folder's form on each OS (a ~ path, an absolute path, a drive or a share, no empty, . or .. segment, no trailing separator, at most 4,096 characters, no control character or lone surrogate), the case rule (Windows and macOS without case, Linux with) and where a folder lands when its parent moves, by whole segments
The folder a launch uses on a machine: the task's own folder there, else its project's folder there, else the machine where the task's or its project's folder is, else none

A folder's stored form on Linux, macOS and Windows: the home written as ~ by whole segments with the OS's case rule, separators made plain, an upper-case drive, a share, the Unicode form kept, and a relative, drive-relative or .. path refused

A look at the disk is timed by the time this process was running: a look of several steps answered while the service was held up before each counts, a look that never answers is given up after its limit and told so, a stall counting as one short tick

The project a working folder belongs to: the deepest project folder that holds it, by whole names and the machine's case rule, exact when it is the project's folder, every project that has that folder, none for a sibling with a longer name; a project folder reached through a link holds the folders of its target

The marker in a project's or a task's folder: the owners' IDs and an ignore file, no task text; a launch's look finds its own marker, another owner's or another space's, a marker gone after it was written from a folder made again at the path, a marker that cannot be read; an old folder without one is marked quietly, and so is the folder that was marked when only its marker went (git clean -x); a marker not written within its bound still keeps the folder and its write lands nothing later, not in a folder moved to the path nor after a clear: one made again at the path asks, and the very folder, also one shared with another owner, takes its marker; Use this folder on a folder that takes no marker is remembered by its identity; what was marked outlives a restart; a folder that takes no marker opens as before; a clear takes the owner off and the last one the marker; a folder moved with another keeps its marker; a checkout's git status stays clean

A folder change whose look at the disk does not answer moves no folder inside the old one and says a folder could not be checked: the old folder's look, the new folder's, its marker's, or one folder's inside the new one

The repository a project's folder holds, by name, from the folder's own Git configuration: origin's or the first remote's, none for no remote, a local remote or a folder that is not a checkout, the name alone for an address with a token, and none when the configuration does not answer in time

Folders through the request path of a running service: a project made for a folder in one change, named after its folder when no name is given; the folder moved on disk with a task's folder and another project's inside it moving along in one change; a folder given another while it is still there leaving the folders inside it, named in the answer; the repository's name in the project list without its address; a folder added again for a project of that name and area answered as that project, a project's folder cleared; a folder inside the TTasks home or a space folder, a missing folder, a file and a relative path refused with nothing written; a retry that replays after the project was renamed; a new project named by several drafts or by calls at once made once; an agent's task filed into an area and project it names first, created with it; a project's folder that does not answer refused in time, holding up no other call of the space, and its late answer writing nothing

Any number of projects on one folder through a running service: projects made for one repository from the page's and the command line's writes, each answer naming the others, a project of the same name and area answered as that one and the same name in another area made; the folder's marker naming every project, an earlier build's marker kept; an agent's status in the folder listing every project's tasks with their project; a new task from the folder in the Inbox with the projects named for an agent bound to no task, and in the bound task's project for a session; one project leaving the folder and the others keeping it; the folder renamed on disk followed for all of them

Folders at the command line: ttasks add and ttasks set give a task its folder with --folder, a folder relative to the working one, folder= and --here, and --clear folder takes it away; --here beside --folder is a usage error; ttasks area create --folder --create makes a folder that is not there and binds it, one undo takes the project, its new area and its folder back and leaves the folder on disk; --folder . --create binds an existing folder; a refused call removes the folder --create made; ttasks area list and ttasks show print the folders

The agent's folder fields through the request path: a task added with folder cwd from a project's subfolder lands in the deepest project whose folder holds it with its own folder, from the project's folder itself takes the project's, from outside every project has no project and its folder, from an archived project's folder has no project, its folder and a warning; a draft that names its group keeps it; a follow-up with folder cwd; a retry replays after the folder went; organize creates a project with its folder, sets it to cwd, lists and clears it, makes a project on a folder another project has and names that one, and makes a project named after the folder when given an area and a folder; cwd without a working folder, a missing folder and the old place field are refused with their reason and the field to use; has:folder and folder: in search; a group an earlier draft makes known by its slug; a refusal's op counting the call's own operations; update_task's folder from cwd

organize's writes through the request path: create a project in a new area, create of what exists answers no_change, create of a name close to another's or of a project another area has makes it while an area named to hold it keeps the typo check, rename keeping the ID with a retry that replays after the rename took the old name, move a project to another area, an area that moves nowhere, archive and unarchive with archive twice no change, and an unknown name not_found

On the 0.2 fixture migrated to 0.3, a task's run written through the write path is detached from its task as entity redaction detaches it (task and request set to null): the space stays intact with no foreign key broken, the detached run reads and still settles through the writer, and the runs table refuses a run with both a task and a routine
